newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Soros says Britain may be wise to wait on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Soros says Britain may be wise to wait on EMU.

text.p: Britain might be wise to wait before joining the European Union's planned single currency because of structural differences between its economy and those of its partners, financier George Soros said on Monday.
"To rush in might be dangerous," he told a news conference at the World Economic Forum in this Swiss mountain resort.
But Soros said that Britain could not afford to stay out permanently, because it had gained much by being a bridge for non-European investment on the continent.
"To stay out permanently would be very damaging," he said.
The single currency -- the euro -- is due to be launched on January 1, 1999, but the British government has yet to decide whether it will take part.
Soros said that the fact that the British economy "danced to a different tune" than those of its European Union partners counselled caution on the timing of a decision to join.
He pointed to the importance of the property market and the country's social security system but without going into details.
